# Leonhard Müllner’s Reports

How can it be possible that one should be able to turn metals into silver and gold so quickly in the molten state—even mercury—when nature itself takes perhaps 1,000 years or longer to work on them until such a thing is accomplished?

To this, I will answer in conclusion: the Medicine <note>The "Philosopher's Stone" or "Tincture," often referred to as a medicine for "sick" or "imperfect" metals.</note> which performs this has attained and received such overflowing perfection and completeness through a long time in the fire. Therefore, as soon as it is cast upon the "unripe" metals in the molten state, it makes them "ripe" and turns them into good silver and gold, according to how the Medicine was prepared.

By what means and path have I come to this secret and art, when so many Emperors, Kings, Electors, and Princes—as well as other Prelates and Lords—have desired this for so long and have not been able to attain it? I swear by God that they have withheld their hands from much labor; therefore, it is only right that they should not know this art. For I have not ceased firing the furnace for twenty years, and have sought after this art with diligence, with labor and reading in the books of the Philosophers <note>original: "Philosophorum" — referring to the ancient and medieval alchemical authorities.</note> day and night without ceasing. I have renounced all worldly joy and pleasure, and have called upon God for it from the heart, early and late. There, I found grace before my God, who revealed such a secret to me through His Holy Spirit and explained this Matter in which this worthy art is hidden. To Him alone be

# Concordance.

<margin>1.</margin> **H**ere the matter of the **Philosophers' Stone** <note>original: "Lapidis Philosophorum"</note> is explained, about which they all write; for all **Philosophers** testify to us concerning the beginning of metals, which occurs from **Salt, Sulfur, and Mercury**, from which all things are composed, whether they be **Vegetable, Animal, or Mineral**, including the metals. Just as the Holy **Trinity of God** exists in three names—as Soul, Body, and Spirit, or **Spirit, Body, and Soul** <note>original: "Spiritus, Corpus & Anima"</note>—yet remains one inseparable essence enclosed in one, from eternity to eternity; so it is also with our matter of the **Stone**, wherein Soul, Body, and Spirit are all enclosed in one, and it is compared by the philosophers to the **Trinity of God**.

<margin>2.</margin> In the **Assembly of the Philosophers** <note>original: "Turba Philosophorum," a famous early Latin alchemical text</note>, or in the Golden Book, mention is made of two **Mercuries**: one that is passive <note>original: "leidet," literally suffers or undergoes</note> and the other that is active <note>original: "würcket," literally works or effects</note>. For the female is passive and the male is active; these two in one matter constitute the <term>Fire</term> <note>The symbol ∆ represents Fire in alchemical notation</note> of the philosophers.

## Truth-loving and most honored
# Reader.

What a man sees with his eyes is, in his opinion, entirely certain; this he knows and believes. And yet, experience shows that he often sees something with his eyes and touches it with his hands, which in his opinion is exactly as he sees and touches it, and yet it does not behave in that way. The cause is his over-subtle and blind reason <note>original: "klügende und blinde Vernunfft"; refers to human intellect that over-analyzes and misses spiritual or natural truths</note>, which he trusts and upon which he builds. On the contrary, he sees with his eyes and touches with his hands that which, according to his own principles, should be entirely certain so that he can grasp it as it is; yet here, it is far too high for him to grasp in his opinion. To recognize the invisible from the visible is a principle <note>original: "Satz"; a philosophical axiom</note> that was indisputable among the heathens <note>original: "Heyden"; likely referring to the ancient Greek and Roman philosophers like Aristotle or Hermes Trismegistus</note>. The metals in the earth, as long as they lie within it, are invisible in their birth <note>original: "Gebährung"; the alchemical process of metals "growing" or being born in the earth's womb</note>; he should recognize them by the visible birth of all things, and yet he complains about the knowledge of the same. # The Generation of Metals

As the process of generation moves forward, so the regeneration moves backward: Take these two lights of the earth <note>Likely referring to Gold (the Sun) and Silver (the Moon)</note>, unite them according to Nature, without the slightest external raw fire, but only with its spiritual fire by means of the cold fire of the ashes. In this way, not even three to four days will pass before you shall immediately see death and the sun darkened, and the mother’s milk flowing. When the father and mother are entirely dead and decayed, then make the dead body living once again, and give it the Water of Life <note>Latin: aqua vitae; here referring to a transformative alchemical solvent</note>. Continue with this until the number of Nature is doubly completed by Nature; then you will find this King in his highest innocence. Let him die away again, and when he is entirely dead, feed and water him again with his milk, and let him appear once more in the second trial of his innocence; thus you can easily glorify him, so that he becomes the King of Glory and of the entire world.

I am not permitted to write more clearly, otherwise one could already point out the beginning and the end printed in the writings of the Sages.

<header>Friederich Roth-Scholtz’s</header>

# Dear Reader!

It will not be necessary to make much boast of the excellence of these few pages; whoever understands the Work, let him give God the glory and praise the Master! The author of this writing was a Swede by birth, named **Josaphat Friederich Hautnorthon**, who, on account of the philosophical secrets and sciences, called himself a son* of the great philosopher, **MICHAEL SENDIVOGIUS**. # Concerning the Third Beginning of Mineral Things.

## The First Chapter.

### The Nature of the Salt of Nature.

Salt is the third beginning <note>The "Three Principles" or Tria Prima of Paracelsian alchemy: Mercury, Sulfur, and Salt.</note> of mineral things, which carries the other two beginnings—namely <term>Mercury</term> and <term>Sulfur</term>—within itself. In its original state, it has the harsh <term>Impression of Saturn</term> <note>In alchemy, Saturn represents lead, coldness, and contraction; it is seen here as the "mother" or formative force of the physical body.</note> as its mother, from which the metals receive their physical bodies. However, this Salt is of three kinds:

First, the **Central Salt**, which is ceaselessly generated in the center of the elements through the qualification of the stars by the <term>Spirit of the World</term> <note>original: "Spiritu Mundi"; the vitalizing universal soul or breath of nature.</note>, and is governed by the rays of the sun and moon in the **Philosophical Sea**.

The second is the **Spermatic Salt**, acting as a housing for the invisible seed. Through a lovely, natural warmth and through <term>putrefaction</term> <note>The process of breaking down or "rotting" matter to release its inner life-force for new growth.</note>, it gives forth its form and growth from within itself—unless that same invisible, volatile seed is driven away by external heat, for in such a case, nothing further can come of it.

The third Salt is the **final matter** of all things, which is found therein after their <term>destruction</term> <note>The reduction of a substance to its ash or base components.</note>. Now, this threefold Salt is thus—

# The Third Chapter.
## Concerning Solution <term>Solution: The process of dissolving a solid substance into a liquid state, seen by alchemists as a "killing" of the metal to release its spirit.</term>.

Solution is the key to the entire Art, and is of three kinds: first, of the raw body <note>original: "Corporis crudi"</note>; secondly, of the Philosophical Earth; and thirdly, in Multiplication <term>Multiplication: The stage where the power of the Alchemical Stone is increased in quantity and quality.</term>. However, because that which has been calcined <note>original: "calciniret"; reduced to powder by heat</note> can be dissolved more easily than that which is uncalcined, it is necessary that the calcination and destruction of the sulfurous impurity <note>original: "impurität"</note> and the combustible stench of the body <note>original: "corporis"</note> must go before. Furthermore, whatever helpful waters or solvents <note>original: "Menstruis"</note> might be used must afterwards be separated from it again, so that absolutely nothing foreign remains with it. This must be done with the highest and most diligent caution, lest—through external heat or other harmful accidents—the innermost generative and multiplicative power <note>original: "vis generativa & multiplicativa"</note> of the Stone be burned, destroyed, and driven away. For the Philosophers <note>original: "Philosophi"</note> in the *Assembly of the Sages* <note>original: "Turba" referring to the *Turba Philosophorum*, one of the oldest European alchemical texts</note> warn most strongly against this, as in Part 1, page 429: "In its purification, you should most of all guard and take care against the deprivation of its power, lest perhaps..."

Once all of this has been united and shaped into a fire-resistant essence, there arises from it the great and powerful **Tincture** <note>A potent alchemical substance, often called the Philosopher's Stone, capable of transforming or "tinging" matter.</note>, which suddenly penetrates the **Bodies** like a powerful flash of lightning and instantly hunts out everything that opposes the core of life. # The Sixth Chapter.

## How the Red Servant is Wedded to the White Woman.

There are many who imagine themselves to be not unlearned in the preparation of the Philosophical Tincture <note>The "Philosophical Tincture" refers to the Elixir or Philosopher's Stone in its liquid, transformative form.</note>; but when our **Red Servant** <note>A symbolic name for Gold or the solar principle (Sulphur) in its active state.</note> examines them, it is almost unbelievable how few in the world can stand the test. For where is there such a book in which one could have perfect instruction on this? Considering that the philosophers have kept this secret, and wished it to remain secret, just as our beloved father left only these few words for researchers as a report: *one single thing mixed with philosophical water* <note>original: "una res sola mixta aqua Philosophica"</note>. Without doubt, this must have given many a philosopher no small amount of work in his first operation to sail past this reef.

In this manner, the disciple of the author of the *Little Peasant* <note>Referring to the alchemical text "Der Kleine Bauer" (The Little Peasant), often attributed to Johann Grasshoff.</note>—who inherited the handwritten manuscripts from his highly esteemed teacher <term>Preceptor</term> <note>A formal term for a teacher or mentor, common in academic and esoteric circles.</note> now resting in God, and who knew the entire Philosophical Art for a full 30 years without any defect—tells us how it fared for his aforementioned teacher in this specific point. For when he came to it for the first time, the two **Sulphurs** <note>The active, combustible principles of the metals being joined.</note> would not mix at all; instead, the **Sun** <note>Gold or the Red Servant.</note> floated upon the **Moon** <note>Silver or the White Woman.</note>.

<summary>This chapter describes the difficult alchemical process of uniting the "Red Servant" (Gold/Sulphur) with the "White Woman" (Silver/Mercury), noting that even experienced masters struggled with the initial mixing of these two principles.</summary>

# Chapter Seven.

## Concerning the Degrees of Fire.

IN the <term>concoction</term> <note>The process of "ripening" or purifying a substance through steady heat.</note> of our salt, the external warmth of the preliminary work is called <term>elixation</term> <note>original: "elixatio"; a process of boiling or softening in liquid.</note>, and it takes place in the moist state. However, the warmth of the subsequent work takes place in the dry state and is called <term>roasting</term> <note>original: "assatio"; a process of heating without added liquid.</note>. These two types of fire are described by the philosophers thus: We must boil and roast the Stone. Furthermore, our blessed work must be conducted according to the constitution of the four seasons of the year: the first period of Winter is cold and moist; the second of Spring is warm and moist; the third of Summer is warm and dry; and the fourth of Autumn is ordained for the gathering of the fruit. 

The warmth of the first stage of governance should be like that of a hen sitting upon her eggs to hatch young chicks, or like that of the stomach which digests food and nourishes the body, or similar to the warmth of manure, or of the sun when it is in <term>Aries</term> <note>original: "Ariete"; the first sign of the zodiac, representing the beginning of Spring.</note>. This warmth lasts until the stage of "blackness" is reached, and also until it is transformed into "whiteness." # Josaphat Friedrich Hautnorthon

## Conclusion.

Here you have, then, the brief contents of the Philosophical Work. Whatever you may still lack, you should seek to discover from the writings and sayings of the ancient Philosophers—which are entirely truthful, and a good portion of which are found in the **Assembly of the Philosophers** <note>original: "Turba Philosophorum," one of the oldest and most influential Latin alchemical texts, presented as a debate between pre-Socratic philosophers</note>. Furthermore, several treatises by the modern Philosophers will explain a great deal to you, such as: **The Sophic Hydrolith** <note>original: "Wasserstein der Weisen," or Water-Stone of the Wise</note>, **THE GLORY OF THE WORLD** <note>original: "GLORIA MUNDI"</note>, the works of **BERNARD OF TREVISO**, **FLAMEL**, **DENIS ZACHAIRE**, and **HOLLANDUS**, among others. 

Above all, however, you must diligently investigate the ground and root of Nature, which you may grasp most fundamentally from the books of the highly enlightened **JACOB BÖHME**, the *Teutonic Philosopher*. In his works, the whole of Nature and her circulation <note>the cyclical movement of spirit and matter</note> stands bare and naked, and can be seized by you—unless, for particular reasons, your eyes are held shut so that your hardened intellect cannot understand it. In itself, however, it is explained so clearly that one must almost be terrified that such high mysteries should be so completely revealed; for all the ancient Sages exhorted most strongly to hide the pearls of wisdom and knowledge from the unworthy, just as every one of them labored to find a special covering to wrap such secrets in and to keep them hidden.

# Josaphat Friedrich Hautnorthon

The debate regarding the **Matter of the Philosopher's Stone** <note>The primary substance needed to begin the Great Work of alchemy.</note> was, before the desired conclusion could be reached, shattered by an unexpected storm and the seekers were scattered into all lands. Each was left to his own long-held opinion because no final decision had been reached. From this, an unspeakable multitude of **sophistical processes** and **alchemical errors** has grown, because every individual worked according to his own delusions and fixed whims. To be sure, some learned alchemists who had been present at that "Imperial Diet" <note>A metaphorical gathering of alchemists or a reference to a specific historical assembly.</note> had read somewhat in the writings of the true Philosophers, where sometimes **Mercury**, sometimes **Sulphur**, and sometimes **Salt** are established by them as the Matter of the Stone. However, because these men understood only common quicksilver, sulfur, and salt, they chose these as the Matter of the Stone and, after their scattering, undertook every imaginable labor therein.

Of this sort was one who had fished out a thought-provoking saying from **Geber** <note>Latinized name of Jabir ibn Hayyan, a foundational figure in alchemy; the quote is likely from the Pseudo-Geber corpus.</note>, where he writes: *The ancient wise men conclude concerning salt, saying it is the soap of the wise and the key which shuts and opens, and shuts again and no one opens; they say that without this little key, no one in this age can arrive at perfection—that is, unless he knows how to calcine the salt after its preparation, and then it is called fusible salt.* <note>original: "Sapientes antiqui concludunt de sale, qui dicunt saponem sapientum & clavem quæ claudit & aperit, & iterum claudit & nemo aperit, sine qua clavicula dicunt neminem in hoc seculo posse pervenire ad perfectionem, id est, nisi sciat salem post suam præparationem calcionare, & tunc dicitur sal fusibilis."</note> And from the **Rosary** <note>Referring to the "Rosarium Philosophorum," a famous 16th-century alchemical series.</note>: *He who knows salt and its solution, he knows the hidden secret of the ancient wise men.* <note>original: "Qui scit salem, & ejus solutionem, ille scit Secretum occultum antiquorum Sapientum."</note> By these sayings, the aforementioned alchemist was led...

He thought, therefore, that common salt would not be the same as what the philosophers mean, but that it must come from the metals themselves. For that reason, he learned to <term>calcine</term><note>To reduce a substance to powder through heat</note> the metals with strong fire, to dissolve them with <term>strong waters</term><note>original: "Aquis fort."; likely nitric acid</note>, to distill, and to prepare salts. He devised many kinds of fluxes to melt the metals, and countless similar vain labors. But in all of this, he could not reach the goal of his desire. Therefore, he began to doubt all such salts and materials again. He leafed through several philosophical books once more, hoping to find perhaps a clear passage that would reveal the <term>Matter</term> to him, until he finally saw the following saying: <note>original: "Lapis noster est Sal, & sal noster est terra, & est terra virginea."</note> *Our Stone is Salt, and our salt is earth, and it is virgin earth.* As he now reflected more deeply upon this, it seemed to him as if a light had suddenly dawned, and he understood now that his aforementioned labors had failed because he had no Virgin Salt, and that such a Virgin Salt could not be found on the surface of the earth

<summary>The text describes an alchemist's transition from working with common salt and metallic acids to seeking the "Virgin Earth" mentioned in Hermetic philosophy. It highlights the trial-and-error nature of early laboratory work and the heavy reliance on interpreting cryptic Latin maxims.</summary>

# Josaphat Friederich Hautnorthon

->The Salt, Sulfur, and Mercury of the Sages.<-

**Alchemist:** How can Salt, Sulfur, and Mercury be one single thing? They are surely three distinct things? **Vision:** Now your foolishness is revealed, and it is clear you still understand nothing. The Sages have only one single thing; it possesses a *Body, Soul, and Spirit* <note>original: "Corpus, Animam & Spiritum"</note>, which they call Salt, Sulfur, and Mercury. All three are present in one single *subject* <note>original: "subjecto"; the underlying material or substance</note>, and that *subject* is their Salt.

**Alchemist:** Where does one obtain such a Salt?

**Vision:** In the dark dungeon of the metals. With it, you can perform wonders and bring all the colors of the world to light; you can also tincture <note>term: tincture; the alchemical process of dyeing or transforming a base metal into a noble one</note> all lesser metals into gold, provided it is first *fixed* <note>term: fixed; rendered stable and non-volatile by fire</note>.

**Alchemist:** But I have long since attempted such works with metals, yet I could never achieve the like?

**Vision:** You sought it in dead metals, which do not contain the power of the Philosophical Seed. Just as you cannot sow baked bread back into the earth, nor hatch a chick from a boiled egg, you must instead have uninjured, living seed for *generation* <note>the process of creation or birth</note>. But the metals of the common man are dead and have no life; why do you seek the living among the dead? <note>A biblical allusion to Luke 24:5, suggesting that ordinary gold is spiritually and chemically "dead" compared to the alchemist's "living" matter.</note>

**Alchemist:** Can gold and silver not be made living again through *solution* <note>term: solution; the process of dissolving a solid into a liquid state</note>?

**Vision:** Philosophical gold and silver are life itself and require no reanimation.

# The First Chapter.
## Concerning the Name.

This Pontic Water is named after the Pontus, or the great World-Ocean, which is said to mean the same as <term>ponos</term> <note>original Greek: πόνος</note> or <term>labor</term> <note>Latin: toil or work</note>, because a laborious path is to be found within it. This Pontus, which is also called the Ocean, is—according to the opinion of <term>Hesiod</term> <note>An ancient Greek poet</note>—the son of Heaven and Earth, and the father of all living things. So too is Venus said to have been sired from the foam of the sea and the blood of Heaven, according to the claim of <term>Tibullus</term> <note>A Roman poet</note>; by which the secret of our Pontic Water, which is called "our Venus" by the Sages, is indicated in a hidden manner.

However, this Pontic Sea-Water is understood in several ways:
I. <term>Properly</term> <note>Latin: propriè</note>, as the great salty World-Ocean.
II. <term>Improperly</term> <note>Latin: impropriè</note>, as the Air, acting as the thinned-out universal sea-water in which we all live, according to the opinion of the author of the *Water-Stone* <note>Referring to the alchemical text "The Water-Stone of the Wise"</note>.
III. <term>Specially</term> <note>Latin: Specialiter</note>, as the Salt-Spirit hidden within such Air, which is also named the Salt of Nature; <term>Sendivogius</term> <note>Michael Sendivogius, a famous Polish alchemist</note> titles it the "Food of Life" hidden in the air.
IV. <term>More Specially</term> <note>Latin: Specialius</note>, as our Philosophical Earth, which captures this Spirit of the Air by <term>magnetic force</term> <note>Latin: vi magnetica</note>. # The Second Chapter.

## Concerning the Description.

From the naming, we now come to the matter itself and its description. The Pontic Water is an airy spirit, attracted by the Philosophical Magnet <note>A substance or force believed by alchemists to draw the "universal spirit" out of the air</note> and resolved into a watery form, in order to accomplish—according to God’s will—the universal masterpiece of the Wise.

It is an airy spirit, for whoever does not know how to cook the air will unfailingly err, says Sendivogius <note>Michael Sendivogius (1566–1636), a famous Polish alchemist and proponent of the theory that life-force exists in the air</note>. This spirit, however, is most conveniently collected in the balsamic months <note>Likely referring to springtime, specifically May and June, when the "universal spirit" was thought to be most potent</note>, as the name Jason is intended to suggest; for he alone was capable of lulling to sleep the fiery dragon lying at Colchis, *near the Black Sea* <note>original: "juxta Pontum"</note>, using a prepared juice. This pure light and Hermetic bird now stands before everyone's eyes, if only the philosophical darkness would comprehend it. According to Khunrath's <note>Heinrich Khunrath (1560–1605), a physician and Hermetic philosopher</note> opinion, such light becomes a salty body and the *salt of wisdom* <note>original: "sal sapientiæ"</note> within the virginal body of our inconspicuous earth. Therefore Hermes writes: Its father is the Sun, its mother the Moon, and the wind (the air) has carried it in its belly, but its nurse is the Earth; its entire power also consists in this: when it is turned into earth. # Chrysogonus de Puris

The *material principles* <note>original: "Principia materialia"</note> of this Earth correspond with those *principles of metals* <note>original: "Principiis metallorum"</note>: For whoever does not know these is far removed from the true Art. Now, the *principles* of metals are: *Sulphur* and *Mercury* <note>The two primary alchemical elements representing the active/combustible and passive/fluid qualities</note>, which are also commonly called Fire and Water, or Man and Woman. These two otherwise opposing natures are united and joined together in our *Salt* or *lime of metals* <note>original: "calce metallorum"</note>, which is the *principle of union*. For the *calcined and soluble substances* are *of the nature of Salts*, says **GEBER** <note>Jabir ibn Hayyan, a foundational 8th-century alchemist</note>, in *Book 1 of the Summary of Perfection, chapter 52.* And in *chapter 25*, he calls the two *principles* a stinking *Spirit*, and a living water; and in *Book 2, chapter 17*, he explains further that our *quicksilver* <note>original: "argentum vivum"</note> is a Salt, *resembling common lime*, because the *Mercury of metals* (as the one *principle*) is transformed through *calcination* <note>the process of heating a substance to high temperatures to drive off volatile matter</note> and *reduction* into a Salt. This Salt, however, has the properties of our *Mercury*, for in it there is *much viscosity, a great deal of dryness, and an earthy stench, so that it is a dry water* <note>original: "aqua sicca"</note>. And in *Book 2, chapter 7*, he also says quite thoughtfully of the other *sulphurous principle*: *Sulphur* is always volatile until it is transformed into Earth, *the likeness of which is of the nature of lime*; therefore **LULL** <note>Ramon Llull, a 13th-century philosopher and purported alchemist</note> also commands in *Experiment 3* to grind <note>original: "trituriren"</note> the blood and to extract a water from it.

# Chrysogonus de Puris

our [Lord]! **O our vegetable! O our fixed and volatile Sulphur! A thing more precious than the whole world.** <note>original: "res omni mundo pretiosior"</note> It is, however, named "fixed Sulphur" on account of the magnetic earth from which it is sublimated; but "volatile" because of the nature of the volatile salt <note>original: "salis naturae"</note>, which unites itself most eagerly with bodies. This occurs to such an extent that, if its desire is not satisfied, this "vegetable" of ours <note>The term "vegetable" here refers to the alchemical growth or life-force of the matter, not a literal plant.</note> separates itself over time from its aqueous vehicle <note>original: "vehiculo aqueo"</note> as a green volatile salt and attaches itself [to the vessel]. In that case, the remaining water afterwards—as experience witnesses—shows mercurial pearl-drops during digestion, but it no longer coagulates into any sulphurous salt. It is thus identical to the separated water from our red urine of the black earth, the composition of which the author of the *Water-Stone* <note>Likely referring to the "Wasserstein der Weisen" or "Water-Stone of the Wise," a famous 17th-century alchemical treatise.</note> has described. For our fountain flows white and red, according to the pleasure of the artist.

This Pontic water <note>A term for a caustic or transformative alchemical solvent.</note> of ours is, firstly, the true radical moisture of metals <note>original: "humidum radicale metallorum"</note>, because on account of its earthly dampness it has remained in the strongest trial of fire <note>original: "in fortissimo ignis examine"</note> and was neither burnt nor fled from it. Instead, according to the testimony of **GEBER** <note>Latinized name of Jabir ibn Hayyan, the foundational 8th-century alchemist.</note> in Book 2 of the *Sum of Perfection*, Chapter 19, it overcomes the heat of the fire, which no other moisture will do. That this is the unique property of the radical moisture of metals is testified by

It cites Geber to prove that this "radical moisture" is the only substance capable of withstanding extreme fire without consuming.</summary>
